candidates.name: Existing Git worktree, commit and merge-tree mechanisms
candidates.fit_for_gap: Preserve source provenance and consolidate histories without directory copying

evidence.claim: Official source repository located via gh search repos; local Git is 2.54.0.
merge-tree inspects committed merge without changing index/worktree; actual simulations retained under research/consolidation/.

risks: Merge simulation omits dirty/untracked changes and does not establish behavior
candidates.decision_rationale: Already installed, sufficient; no added consolidation framework.

candidates.name: Existing KBD canonical state and replica/conflict interfaces
candidates.fit_for_gap: Resolve mini generated projection conflicts without choosing one worktree's process history

evidence.claim: Installed prometheus kbd help exposes replicas, conflicts, resolve, status and typed phase/stage transitions; mini conflicts are current-waypoint.json and position.json.

risks: Canonical state/replica evidence must be preserved separately from Git
Operator-signed adjudication may be required for genuine conflicts
candidates.decision_rationale: Preserve one shipping identity; independent convergence KBD identity remains separate.

candidates.name: Existing integration-sources and tool/payload manifests
candidates.fit_for_gap: Bind source baseline, dependency closure and actual binaries across repositories

evidence.claim: Active Boss build/integration-sources.json pins UAR c29af47be3 and mini 86b2c7e1a7 while active source has later changes; UAR vendor Liter pin differs from mini.

risks: Manifest consistency alone does not prove deployed binary provenance
Operator-authored versions.toml cannot be silently edited
candidates.decision_rationale: Extend existing manifest contracts, avoid a new registry or daemon.

candidates.name: Codex Rust prepared execution and correlated approval
candidates.fit_for_gap: Approval/execution identity and live pending-request recovery

evidence.claim: Local Codex 986ff1cc7ced: core tools/approvals.rs, tools/orchestrator.rs, codex-mcp/binding.rs and app-server/outgoing_message.rs inspected; integrated landscape report includes source links.

risks: Not a drop-in cross-process Boss authorization receipt
Live callback replay does not guarantee crash continuation or exactly-once effects
candidates.decision_rationale: Closest inspected Rust reference; adapt concepts within existing UAR after baseline consolidation.

candidates.name: Wholesale merge or directory-copy every worktree

evidence.claim: UAR presentation merge has 80 conflicted paths before dirty work; local configuration and generated files coexist with product WIP.

risks: Can resurrect obsolete behavior, lose WIP/identity, or publish private local config
candidates.decision_rationale: Explicit feature recovery and archive disposition are faster and more reliable than absorbing every experiment.

candidates.name: Runtime-owned broker with monotonic Boss host admission

evidence.claim: UAR existing broker and Ask preservation; Boss controller disposition and bridge ledger documented in assessment/local evidence.

risks: Host auto must not downgrade UAR Ask; independent host deny remains final.
candidates.decision_rationale: Extend existing coordinator and adapter; one human decision, independently enforced host restrictions.

candidates.name: Prepared invocation and managed MCP metadata admission

evidence.claim: Pinned rmcp 3.1.2 CallToolRequestParams exposes _meta; Codex prepared bindings and current Boss FIFO bridge inspected.

risks: Metadata is not authority without authenticated control exchange, stored binding and atomic single consumption.
candidates.decision_rationale: Use immutable invocation binding and host-issued opaque admission on existing managed channel; no external server schema change.

candidates.name: Safe renderer presentation and opaque decision replies

evidence.claim: Assessment source traces distinguish raw tool arguments from pending decision correlation; Codex app-server maps pending reply IDs.

risks: Over-redaction hides effects; insufficient redaction leaks credentials; renderer must not replace arguments.
candidates.decision_rationale: Main-process safe display projection with meaningful targets; allow/deny only, edits require a new invocation.

candidates.name: Live pending replay with cancellation and epoch invalidation

evidence.claim: UAR root/child broker, generation and SSE cursor exist; Codex outgoing request map and pending replay inspected.

risks: A live waiter cannot survive process loss; post-dispatch effects may be outcome-unknown.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reuse live continuations and single-consumption decisions; invalidate on process restart, audit interruption, no automatic write replay.

candidates.name: Transparent durable restart and approval-time mutation

evidence.claim: Inspected Codex replay concerns live callbacks, not a universal durable external-effects transaction.

risks: Would require durable execution/idempotency contracts across arbitrary tools and revalidation after argument edits.
candidates.decision_rationale: Defer transparent crash continuation; new invocation for edited actions or intentional retry.

build_required.need: Create scoped recoverable product checkpoints and reconcile dirty work before main integration
build_required.why_no_candidate: Git preserves objects but cannot determine user intent or whether a legacy feature supersedes current behavior.

build_required.need: Reconcile Liter host credential isolation, streaming WIP and actual UAR/mini consumer pins
build_required.why_no_candidate: Three HTTP transport conflicts and distinct consumer requirements need repository-specific integration.

build_required.need: Record source/binary/config provenance and exercise one complete catalog-to-MCP integration boundary
build_required.why_no_candidate: No source-management tool can establish runtime behavior from branch names or successful textual merges.

build_required.need: Implement the bounded UAR/Boss admission adapter and safe renderer decision projection
build_required.why_no_candidate: Codex patterns and rmcp metadata support the design but neither implements this repository-specific trust boundary.
